title: Claude Fable 5 Launch and Enterprise Admin Permissions
description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5, a Mythos-class model safe for general use. Additionally, Enterprise plans can now manage admin permissions with custom roles, extending the existing framework by adding admin functionality for billing, privacy, and other administrative areas.

community_feedback.quote: Claude Fable 5 ranks at 65 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, ahead of GPT-5.5 (60) and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (57)
The most capable model Anthropic has ever made generally available

title: Enterprise Custom Roles Framework Extended
description: Enterprise plans can manage admin permissions with custom roles. The update extends the existing custom roles framework by adding admin permissions, giving members access to specific administrative areas without requiring Owner status.

title: Bugbot Performance Improvements - 3x Faster
description: Bugbot is now over 3x faster, 22% cheaper, and finds 10% more bugs. The average review time dropped from ~5 minutes to ~90 seconds. Performance gains are powered by Composer 2.5 training progress.

title: Cursor SDK Enhancements - Custom Tools and Auto-Review
description: Released new functionality across TypeScript and Python SDKs including custom stores (SQLite and JSONL), custom tools via function definitions, auto-review for local agents, and nested subagents support. Includes reliability and performance fixes for production use.

community_feedback.quote: Independent PSF assessment of Cursor SDK 3.7 covers custom tools implementation, auto-review functionality for headless runs, nested subagents, and JSONL stores

title: Codex App 26.608 - Migration Flows and Plugin Revamp
description: Added 'Migrate to Codex' flows for importing setups from Claude Code and Claude Cowork during onboarding. Revamped plugins screen with separate tabs, marketplace filters, keyboard navigation, and clearer install actions. Expanded Settings search across more panels.

title: Sites Feature Preview - Build and Deploy Websites
description: Sites is now available in preview in the Codex app, allowing users to create, save, deploy, and inspect websites, dashboards, internal tools, web apps, and games hosted by OpenAI. ChatGPT Business workspaces include Sites by default.

title: Amazon Bedrock Support
description: Codex can now use supported OpenAI models available through Amazon Bedrock. Users can configure Amazon Bedrock as their model provider to run Codex locally with AWS-managed authentication, account controls, and billing.

title: Terminal Placement Controls
description: Added 'Default terminal location' in General settings. When the bottom panel is enabled, users can choose whether terminal shortcuts and environment actions open in the bottom panel or right panel.

title: Gemini CLI Discontinuation Announcement
description: Google announced that Gemini CLI will be discontinued on June 18, 2026 for all user tiers (free, Pro, and Ultra). This will affect CI/CD pipelines, shell scripts, automation tools, and any system calling the Gemini CLI. A migration guide is available for users.

community_feedback.quote: Gemini CLI will stop working from June 18, 2026
Gemini CLI was considered 'far behind' both Claude Code and Codex

title: Gemini 2.0 Model Shutdown
description: Google shut down gemini-2.0-flash and gemini-2.0-flash-001 models on June 1, 2026. Users were advised to migrate to newer model versions.

title: Usage-Based Billing and GitHub Actions Integration
description: GitHub Copilot moved to usage-based billing on June 1, 2026, where costs depend on the model used and usage amount. Copilot code review began consuming GitHub Actions minutes starting the same day. Several legacy models were also deprecated.

community_feedback.quote: End of an Era - Reddit discussion title indicating strong sentiment about the changes
Developers concerned about moving from predictable, flat-rate pricing to a variable consumption model that could make costs harder to forecast and budget
Unpredictability in costs - moving from fixed-price subscriptions to variable usage-based billing creates budget planning difficulties
